claims.text: The heterostructure includes grain-size distributions, interphase boundaries, and secondary-phase morphologies.
An integrated digital twin coupling high-resolution microstructural imaging with machine learning can predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior.
The proposed digital twin will be more accurate than traditional finite-element or atomistic simulations.
The proposed digital twin will be faster than traditional finite-element or atomistic simulations.
SEM and micro-CT imaging can provide quantitative descriptors of grain-size distributions, interphase boundaries, and secondary-phase morphologies.
Supervised machine-learning models can map those microstructural descriptors to bulk mechanical properties.
Models trained on paired microstructural measurements and mechanical-test data can rapidly interpolate stress–strain and fracture behavior.
Machine-learning interpolation reduces reliance on computationally intensive physics-based simulations.
Embedding physics-based constraints helps the framework capture damage initiation and propagation.
The framework is predicted to improve predictive accuracy by approximately 15–20%.
Predicted mechanical-property values are expected to fall within 5–10% of experimental measurements.
The framework is predicted to reduce computational simulation time by 30–40% relative to conventional finite-element approaches.
The approach may fail when the captured descriptors omit microstructural features governing damage.
Model overfitting may prevent generalization across tensile and fracture conditions.
Consistent prediction errors greater than 10% across multiple independent samples and test conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
